title: Charging up and catching your fall
target: How the charging station and the tumble-wings upgrade work in R.E.P.O., so a battery is topped up knowingly and a fall is survived on purpose.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A charging station in the shop
The tumble wings bought, if you have them

steps.do: Put the item in the station rather than beside it.
steps.because: the station has a body and a subtle light, and it takes an item (ChargingStation, meshObject, subtleLight, item)

steps.do: Read the bar while it charges, because charging is drawn in segments.
steps.because: it charges in segments along a curve and lights a bar of its own (chargeSegments, chargeCurve, barLight)

steps.do: Know that a crystal can break, and that it is audible.
steps.because: it holds a crystal cylinder and a set of crystals, and it has a sound for a power crystal breaking (crystalCylinder, crystals, soundPowerCrystalBreak)

steps.do: Do not stand in the beam.
steps.because: it works with a laser mesh, a laser point and a line drawn between two points (chargeLaserMesh, laserPoint, chargeLaser, LineBetweenTwoPoints)

steps.do: Remember the wings belong to your avatar rather than to an item slot.
steps.because: the upgrade refers to the player avatar it belongs to (ItemUpgradePlayerTumbleWingsLogic, playerAvatar)

steps.do: Expect the wings to be built from a left and a right.
steps.because: the wings have a transform of their own with a left and a right wing transform (transformWings, transformWingLeft, transformWingRight)

steps.do: Use the light and the sound to tell whether the wings are out.
steps.because: there is a light belonging to the wings and a looping sound played from a local audio source (lightWings, soundWingsLoop, localAudioSource)

commonMistakes: Leaving an item next to the station and assuming it charged.
Forgetting that the wings are an avatar upgrade rather than a carried tool.
Missing that the wings are lit and audible, and so can be checked without looking.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
